text:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT (SEV2) - us-east-2 streaming endpoints showing bursty 5xx and connection resets. Initial impact ~5% of streaming sessions; increased tail latency for some customers. Investigating possible thundering-herd on kv-cache misses.

zara (oncall): taking this. paging runtime, edge. seeing large spike in cache_miss_rate and simultaneous refill operations. grabbing metrics and logs.

leo (runtime): noted a massive fanout to the cache after warmup for several PLG apps around 13:05 UTC. suspect missing jitter on background populate path.

ben (edge): surface-level: edge-proxy shows connection reset count up x4 and many simultaneous replays to origin:
```
# jq ".requests | select(.time>\"2026-07-11T13:05:00Z\") | .path, .status" edge-proxy.log | head -n 10"/v1/stream", 502"/v1/stream", 502"/v1/stream", 504"/v1/stream", 502
```

support-ops: drafting status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/204567 - "Investigating elevated streaming errors in US-EAST-2. Partial customer impact, mitigation underway."

zara (oncall): correlation: a scheduled TTL reduction job ran at 12:58 UTC that removed a lot of small entries, causing many clients to simultaneously repopulate prefixes. no hard eviction cap prevented concurrent refills.

leo (runtime): mitigation plan: 1) enable soft-rate-limit on cache-populate RPCs (per-caller token-bucket), 2) enable jittered backoff on populate, 3) route heavy clients to degraded-model variant if they exceed populate retries. Preparing canary.

ben (edge): can we also throttle at edge for identical hot prefixes? I'll add a small per-prefix coalescing layer to dedupe refill requests.

leo (runtime): applying canary: soft-rate-limit=200rps per-populate, jitter=0-200ms, coalesce-window=50ms on pool stream-workers-4-canary.

infra-bot: canary metrics snapshot after 90s: cache_populate_rps canary 320->90, populate_fail_rate 18%->4%, streaming_5xx on canary 6.2%->0.7%.

zara (oncall): good signal. proceeding staged rollout 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 2m observation windows. status page update: partial mitigation observed.

support-ops: CS notified. Two enterprise customers live-demo impacted; CS lead oncall for updates.

ben (edge): coalescing layer reduced duplicate origin hits by ~82% on canary. will roll with runtime change.

leo (runtime): rolling to 50% now. if we see >1.5% 5xx we pause. also enabling temporary circuit-breaker to fail fast for clients doing >10 populates/s.

zara (oncall): after 3 phases overall streaming 5xx dropped 5.0% -> 0.9%; connection resets reduced. still monitoring tail latencies for a few heavy tenants.

cs-lead: communicated to affected enterprise customers: mitigation in progress; follow-up postmortem promised.

leo (runtime): deploying follow-up fix: add hard mem cap and eviction-safety that prevents unbounded growth during mass repopulation. PR queued and will ship after incident.

support-ops: status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/204567 - "Mitigation in place; most customers recovered. Engineering working on permanent fix."

zara (oncall): RESOLVED at 2026-07-11T13:46:39Z. Streaming 5xx returned to baseline and tail latencies normalized. Postmortem thread and action items created (add jitter to populate path, add per-prefix coalescing in edge, hard caps + circuit-breaker on kv-cache).

sre-bot: Incident update posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/204567 - Resolved. RCA and action tracker forthcoming. :white_check_mark:
